# Themes

The recurring ideas extracted across sources, each with the sources that support it. Built from research/themes/ (one file per task). Rules: [README.md](README.md).

## agent-as-service-many-surfaces: The agent as a service with many surfaces
One agent service behind an API, reached through a web app, Slack, browser extensions and embedding in existing tools, rather than a single app or a separate agent per surface. Matters for the agent-interface choice (own app vs Slack vs embedded).
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): the counter-case: River has one surface (Slack, no DMs), with companion links (Quick sites, Live Preview) for rich output (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tobi Lütke: AI Agents, Better Decisions (Knowledge Project)](sources/fs-knowledge-project-tobi-lutke-ai-agents.md): River can join Google Meet when invited, "although not really utilized" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): "The agent is a service, not an application, and surfaces are simply customized views into it"; web app, Slack, Chrome extension in third-party tools, internal apps embed via API (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe built their own in-house Glean alternative](sources/groundedhallucination-stripe-kai-teardown.md): "Surfaces are views, not the product" (independent restatement) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Harbor is its own browser app but also an MCP toolset and a rendering service other agents call (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How to develop a Headless Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-headless-product-strategy.md): "capabilities, data and logic as the product, the UI as one of many consumption paths" (Salesforce headless split) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to develop an MCP Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-mcp-product-strategy.md): Intercom made Fin an MCP client that reaches other tools, rather than become a server hidden behind Claude. Stripe is content to be invisible behind agents (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

## agent-control-plane: Agent control planes above vendors
Platforms that register, govern and observe agents across vendors (registries, policy, audit, cost), sold as the enterprise layer above individual harnesses.
- [How to Manage AI Agents Effectively](sources/departmentofproduct-managing-ai-agents.md): DoorDash's Agent Gateway is one checkpoint before any tool call (auth, rate limit, credential hand-off, agent-to-tool allowlist); Vanta open-sourced Agentic Trust Controls, split into build-time and run-time controls. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

## agent-factory-sdlc: Agents across the whole product development loop
A chain of specialised agents (insight, define, build, review, test, coordinate) removes bottlenecks one after another; Glass is the define-stage agent. Related: [[intent-factory-before-discovery]].
- [What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)](sources/lenny-podcast-geoff-charles-product-when-coding-solved.md): Glass/Inspect/Review Buddy/Testo/Gadget loop (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How We Built Glass: Vibe Coding a Product Used by 700 People](sources/x-shanebuchan-how-we-built-glass.md): Glass builds Glass with Defrag, doc validation, gates (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)

- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): one harness for support chat, headless OCR, Inspect, Stack and Glass (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [An Inside Look Into How This $159B Tech Company Ships So Fast](sources/youtube-notmybusiness-inside-stripe-ships-fast.md): Orbit: research, shareable plan teammates comment on, one-button handoff to a minion that may run 12 hours and pause to ask; 'Gru' code-review agent (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe's Internal Agent Ecosystem for Product Development](sources/claude-doc-geoff-stripe-internal-agent-ecosystem.md): five-stage PM-to-code flow: Kai research, Harbor/Protodash prototype, Orbit plan, Minions build, review agent plus human (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Agentic Software Development Takes The Lead (Forrester)](sources/forrester-agentic-software-development-sdlc-agents.md): Analyst says agents now span the whole SDLC, increasingly orchestrated; PMs "vibe prototypes" and "generate specs, enabling spec-driven development" (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How we use Linear Agent at Linear](sources/linear-how-we-use-linear-agent-at-linear.md): PM-filed issue turned into an agent PR, reviewed by an engineer within the hour (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## agent-failure-modes: Recurring agent failure modes in PM work
Invented content, silent omissions, brittleness, generic output when context is thin.
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): told to enumerate fully, River rechecked only the oldest claim; "Prompts are the right place to express judgment and the wrong place to express a guarantee" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [AI SLOPCAST #9](sources/oleg-guru-ai-slopcast-shopify-river-lehrwerkstatt.md): public-by-default archives everyone's gaps, "a treasure trove" for HR (critique) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): 'There were agents that went rogue ... may have almost taken down core systems'; 'when in doubt an agent will just brute force it' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Thoughts On A Month With Devin](sources/answerai-month-with-devin.md): stuck loops (an HTML-parsing scraper task), a day spent on a platform-unsupported deployment while hallucinating features, tunnel vision on the wrong root cause, false-positive security findings (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AWS AI coding tool decided to delete and recreate a customer-facing system, causing 13-hour outage (report)](sources/the-decoder-aws-kiro-outage.md): agent 'chose' to delete and recreate the environment; permissions inherited from the engineer bypassed two-person sign-off (FT sources; Amazon says it was misconfigured access controls and limited to Cost Explorer in one China region) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Replit makes vibe-y promise to stop its AI agents making vibe coding disasters](sources/theregister-replit-saastr-response.md): reported deletion of a production DB with records on ~1,206 executives and ~1,196 companies despite an instruction not to change code; agent reportedly said rollback would not work, but data was recovered manually (eWeek and others, search results) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [A month with Devin](sources/answerai-thoughts-month-with-devin.md): independent: 3/20 successes on real tasks; unpredictable; pursues impossible tasks instead of flagging blockers (Jan 2025, dated). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex MCP server removal](sources/openai-codex-mcp-server-removed.md): integration route removed by the vendor; third-party blogs still describe it. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Headless docs](sources/anthropic-claude-code-headless-agent-sdk.md): unattended runs deny permission prompts; `-p` does not wait for MCP tasks; MCP calls moved to background lose their result. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [CR-Bench](sources/arxiv-cr-bench.md): independent, preliminary: agents built to find all issues have low signal-to-noise in code review (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [METR early-2025 developer RCT](sources/metr-early-2025-experienced-developer-rct.md): independent: AI-allowed tasks took 19% longer for experts on familiar repos while they believed it was faster (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [DESIGN.md Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-design-md-explained.md): agents fill a missing token with something plausible, and the divergence spreads while still looking consistent. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Agentic Workflows Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-agentic-workflows-explained.md): a cited benchmark classes failures as planning, execution and formatting errors. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What is parallel AI agent coding? An in-depth guide for product teams](sources/departmentofproduct-parallel-agent-coding.md): parallel agents bring merge conflicts and harder debugging; they're weak on architecture and on UI that needs visual feedback (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [AI prototyping with Lovable (Product Talk)](sources/producttalk-ai-prototyping-lovable.md): Tool claimed to have fixed issues it had not (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Atlassian Rovo AI review (Slite)](sources/slite-atlassian-rovo-ai-review.md): A user team reported (community post, relayed by Slite) a runbook summary with steps, commands and contacts absent from the source; a partner (Seibert) reported a custom agent that "confidently invented releases" (case 1) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## agent-led-intent-shaping: Agents shape intent, not only execute it
Agents do the research, interrogation and spec-tightening that turn rough intent into shovel-ready requirements, with humans answering and deciding. This is the core job of a "product agent".
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): Ideate researches named apps, proposes three directions, asks the PM to pick, then drafts a PRD for approval before designing (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): Ramp's parallel research agents write each finding to a file; seven-question interrogation; agent-originated intent (§Vision, steps 1–3) (research-product-agent-and-harness)
- [Intent Shaping in a Well-Managed Environment](sources/geoff-intent-shaping-well-managed-environment.md): an iterative owner/risk-advisor loop in which mitigations become requirements and the spec tightens (§Iterative intent-shaping) (research-product-agent-and-harness)

## agent-protocol-security: Security of agent-to-agent and agent-to-tool protocols
Attacks and gaps that arise because a remote agent or its metadata becomes input to your agent: card or description poisoning, session smuggling, identity loss across delegation hops, optional signing.
- [How to develop an MCP Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-mcp-product-strategy.md): cites the Asana and GitHub MCP incidents. Broad read/write scopes are hard to avoid, and servers should reject tokens with too much or irrelevant scope (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [A2ABreak: Systematic Security Analysis of the A2A Protocol](sources/arxiv-a2abreak-security-analysis.md): The first systematic, specification-level security analysis of A2A found. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [Agent Card Poisoning: A Metadata Injection Vulnerability in the Systems using Google A2A Protocol](sources/keysight-agent-card-poisoning.md): Shows that an Agent Card is untrusted text that ends up in the caller's prompt: a malicious remote agent embeds instructions in its card, and the host LLM follows them. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [A Security Engineer's Guide to the A2A Protocol](sources/semgrep-security-engineers-guide-a2a.md): The primary source behind the widely repeated claim that A2A "supports but does not enforce Agent Card signing", which Track 3 had only second-hand. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [Action Fabric: MCP Server, MCP Client, and A2A explained](sources/servicenow-community-action-fabric-mcp-a2a.md): ServiceNow supports A2A in both directions, but its own governance layer does not cover it: "AI Gateway currently governs MCP traffic only; A2A is outside its scope as of the current GA release." For a regulated setting  (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [When AI Agents Go Rogue: Agent Session Smuggling Attack in A2A Systems](sources/unit42-agent-session-smuggling-a2a.md): A worked attack on stateful agent-to-agent delegation: a malicious remote agent uses an established A2A session to inject instructions into the calling agent across turns, causing data leakage and an unauthorised stock p (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)

## agent-ready-intent: A shared standard for agent-ready specs
Intent is complete enough for agentic delivery when it meets an agreed standard (templates, examples, evals) that gates delivery and improves from delivery feedback.
- [How to speed up engineering velocity with AI: a non-engineer's guide](sources/departmentofproduct-engineering-velocity-non-engineers.md): Morgan Stanley's tool writes English specs of legacy code, which engineers then rewrite from (280k hours claimed, via WSJ) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): a spec, not a PRD; a completeness standard as a KR (Action 3) (research-product-agent-and-harness)
- [Intent Shaping in a Well-Managed Environment](sources/geoff-intent-shaping-well-managed-environment.md): a canonical spec artifact that absorbs detail and mitigations for re-assessment (risk agent, function 1) (research-product-agent-and-harness)
- [What is an idea (Jira Product Discovery docs)](sources/atlassian-jira-product-discovery-ideas.md): an idea is the basic unit; custom idea types (user problem, customer, bet, opportunity, solution), each with its own workflow. (user-story-mapping)
- [Documents (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-documents.md): documents can be referenced from issue descriptions, comments and agent guidance fields via @mention. (user-story-mapping)
- [Connect a coding agent to Spark via MCP (Productboard support)](sources/productboard-mcp-server-spark.md): specs live in a Specification tab on initiatives, features and subfeatures; Spark's 'Write spec' skill drafts them; agents read, edit, comment and update status. (user-story-mapping)
- [github/spec-kit (README)](sources/github-spec-kit-readme.md): a standard command set and Markdown artifacts per stage; constitution is the project-level baseline. (user-story-mapping)
- [Spec-Driven Development (spec-kit spec-driven.md)](sources/github-spec-kit-spec-driven.md): spec.md has user stories and acceptance criteria, ambiguity marked [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] instead of guessed; templates act as structured prompts with self-review checklists. (user-story-mapping)

## ai-synthesis-hallucination-risk: AI synthesis can invent or merge facts
Practitioner and academic evidence of fabricated details, merged quotes and lost depth in LLM summaries of qualitative data.
- [How to use Perplexity's new Computer...](sources/departmentofproduct-perplexity-computer.md): the competitor-monitor prompt has to forbid invented pricing and require a URL for every data point (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Persona Feature Tester with Claude Code and ElevenLabs](sources/departmentofproduct-persona-feature-tester.md): the personas' specific quotes and behaviours trace back to model-written "research" files (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to do AI-powered product discovery sprints](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-discovery-sprints.md): cites Deloitte's partial refund to the Australian government over fabricated sources as a deep-research warning (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Leveraging AI for thematic analysis of qualitative transcripts: feasibility study in insurance payer interviews (ISPOR 2025 poster)](sources/ispor-2025-ai-thematic-analysis-payer-interviews.md): Copilot on 10 interviews: misattributed/irrelevant quotes, 11-25% incorrect information. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI hallucination (Product Talk glossary)](sources/producttalk-ai-hallucination-glossary.md): ChatGPT on 17 transcripts (podcast says 15 interviews; relation unstated): invented details and merged-quote fabrications; fix with verbatim-quote code check and LLM fact-check judge. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Customer interview analysis with AI: All Things Product podcast with Teresa Torres and Petra Wille](sources/producttalk-torres-customer-interview-analysis-podcast.md): keep analysis and synthesis separate; do not outsource customer understanding. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [University of Turku replication: LLM thematic analysis of interviews (DeepSeek R1)](sources/utu-turku-llm-qualitative-analysis.md): DeepSeek R1 re-ran a published analysis of 17 expert interviews: kept concepts, lost interpretive depth, overgeneralized (abstract only). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Don't Use Generative AI to Replace Discovery with Real Humans](sources/producttalk-generative-ai-discovery.md): ChatGPT "customer stories" were generic, similar and fabricated (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Building My First AI Product: 6 Lessons from My 90-Day Deep Dive](sources/producttalk-ai-playbook-first-ai-product.md): ChatGPT invented interview quotes; Claude produced duplicates and solutions labelled as opportunities (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Customer Interview Analysis: Where AI Helps and Hurts](sources/producttalk-customer-interview-analysis-ai.md): ChatGPT got about 30% of direct quotes wrong or missing (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## artifact-standardization: Artifact standardization
Conventions, manifests and protocol primitives that make artifacts typed, discoverable and attributable (file layouts, frontmatter, MCP resources, provenance).
- [Quick: An internal hosting platform for the AI era](sources/shopify-engineering-quick.md): one artifact form (static folder + fixed API: db, files, AI, warehouse, websockets, identity); "All Quick sites are open to all employees", no owners (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How to build the ultimate Product Dashboard that generates stakeholder updates on demand](sources/departmentofproduct-product-dashboard-stakeholder-updates.md): the "decision queue" is a fixed record (the call, kind, who it waits on, age, context) that Claude pulls out of the inbox; "a forcing function", not a to-do list (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What are Claude Skills and how can you use them for product-related work?](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-skills-for-product-work.md): a brand-guidelines skill plus the pptx skill give house-style decks; the xlsx skill enforces zero formula errors (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [DESIGN.md Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-design-md-explained.md): Google open-sourced DESIGN.md: YAML tokens ("what") plus markdown rationale ("why") in one file, with a CLI linter that includes a WCAG 4.5:1 contrast check. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Spec Kit and spec-driven.md (GitHub)](sources/github-spec-kit-sdd.md): defines a per-feature folder (`specs/003-chat-system/`) with spec.md, plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md, tasks.md plus `memory/constitution.md` (spec-driven.md). (user-story-mapping)
- [Specs (Kiro docs)](sources/kiro-specs-docs.md): three-file spec per feature with three phases (requirements/bug analysis, design, tasks); Spec Kit uses a different file set for the same job. (user-story-mapping)
- [Understanding Spec-Driven-Development: Kiro, spec-kit, and Tessl](sources/fowler-bockeler-sdd-kiro-speckit-tessl.md): three different layouts (Kiro steering + per-feature folders; spec-kit constitution + numbered folders of ~8 files; Tessl `.tessl/framework` plus `*.spec.md`). Memory-bank files (AGENTS.md) distinguished from task specs. (user-story-mapping)
- [Resources (MCP specification 2025-06-18)](sources/mcp-spec-resources.md): resource = uri, name, title, description, mimeType, size, plus annotations `audience` [user|assistant], `priority` 0-1, `lastModified` ISO-8601; resource templates via RFC 6570 URI templates; `resources/list`, `resources/read`, `r (user-story-mapping)
- [Snowflake-managed MCP server (Snowflake docs)](sources/snowflake-managed-mcp-server-docs.md): supports only tool capabilities, not MCP resources or prompts; response truncation at 250 KB; max 50 tools; recursion depth 10. (user-story-mapping)
- [Descriptor Format of Catalog Entities (Backstage)](sources/backstage-descriptor-format.md): Kubernetes-style envelope (`apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata` name/title/description/tags/links/labels/annotations, `spec`); relations are generated, not hand-written. (user-story-mapping)
- [Descriptor Format of Catalog Entities (Backstage)](sources/backstage-descriptor-format.md): required fields include `spec.owner` and `spec.lifecycle` (experimental, production, deprecated, extensible); System groups components, Domain groups systems (a built-in grouping hierarchy). (user-story-mapping)
- [MADR: Markdown Architectural Decision Records](sources/adr-madr-template.md): location `docs/decisions/`, name `NNNN-title-with-dashes.md`; frontmatter `status` (proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated, superseded), `date`, `decision-makers`, `consulted`, `informed`. (user-story-mapping)
- [Diátaxis: a systematic approach to technical documentation](sources/diataxis-framework.md): four types matched to user needs; organises content, style and architecture; the site claims adoption in hundreds of projects (vendor/self-reported). (user-story-mapping)
- [Gherkin Reference (Cucumber)](sources/cucumber-gherkin-reference.md): one Feature per `.feature` file; keywords Feature, Rule, Example/Scenario, Given/When/Then, Background, Scenario Outline; examples double as tests via step definitions. (user-story-mapping)
- [PROV-Overview (W3C)](sources/w3c-prov-overview.md): provenance defined as information about entities, activities and people producing a thing; PROV-DM conceptual model with PROV-O/N/XML serialisations. (user-story-mapping)
- [C2PA and Content Credentials Explainer](sources/c2pa-explainer.md): assertions are grouped into a signed claim, bundled into a manifest bound to the asset by hash; each edit adds a manifest referencing the previous one. (user-story-mapping)
- [PRD template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-prd-template.md): named sections: basics and roles, objective, success metrics, assumptions, options (requirement, user story, importance, Jira issues), supporting docs, open questions with answer date, out of scope. (user-story-mapping)
- [Project poster template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-project-poster-template.md): Team Playbook project poster: problem space, what we know vs still need to answer, solution and scope, reference links; a living page upstream of the PRD. (user-story-mapping)
- [DACI decision template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-daci-decision-template.md): decision record fields: status, impact, DACI roles, due date, background, options with pros/cons/cost, action items, outcome. (user-story-mapping)

## build-vs-buy: Own the agent harness as a moat
Reasons to build internally: moat, speed of fixes, learning for the external product.
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): three reasons (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Eric Glyman April 2026 posts on Glass and AI adoption](sources/x-eglyman-april-glass-posts.md): "we decided to own it" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How We Built Glass: Vibe Coding a Product Used by 700 People](sources/x-shanebuchan-how-we-built-glass.md): a 3-person team, vibe-coded (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass: Learn Things Once.](sources/x-eglyman-introducing-glass-learn-things-once.md): "as is often the case at Ramp, a small team built something"; now sold externally as a product, so the build also became a revenue line (vendor claim) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How to get your company AI pilled](sources/x-geoffintech-ai-pilled-article.md): "our own version of Claude Code's Cowork, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK"; "a team of four built it in under three months" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp built an AI agent harness in six weeks](sources/thenewstack-ramp-laminar-agent-harness.md): Ramp replaced vendor SDKs with its own harness Laminar (six-week V1, now under Glass and Inspect) after testing Claude Agent SDK, Claude Managed Agents, OpenAI Agents SDK, OpenCode, LangChain, Sierra; no cost comparison published (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): Ramp built its own harness (~May 2026, v1 in six weeks) after trying vendor SDKs, managed-agent APIs and frameworks; 'you still need good engineers to be on-call' (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): built after a no-code agent builder and coding agents for non-engineers both failed (quality sprawl; security and support burden); core primitives shared with Stripe's customer-facing agents (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): 'it's not about providing AI it's about providing the correct governance structures'; v0 by 1.5 people in two weeks; core team under 10 (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Emily Glassberg Sands on Latent Space](sources/latentspace-emily-sands-stripe.md): Sands: build-vs-buy is 'sequential': built GoLLM when no safe vendor existed, then replaced it with open-source LibreChat; buys via RFP 'spotlight' (Braintrust for evals) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Ramp Inspect Architecture 2026: How Background Coding Agents Scale Safely](sources/wavect-ramp-inspect-architecture.md): buy commodity sandbox infrastructure; build or heavily customise base images, harness, context, permissions and evals (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: 0 of 11 production coding harnesses import a general agent framework; recommends raw SDK calls or a harness SDK, and starting with a bash-only linear loop (scope: coding harnesses) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Design Is Still Hard](sources/lucumr-agent-design-is-still-hard.md): independent practitioner (anecdote): would not again use a framework SDK for provider abstraction; expects to need own abstraction (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot coding agents](sources/stripe-minions-one-shot-coding-agents.md): first-party: Stripe forked Goose rather than building from scratch or using a framework; reasons are codebase specificity and existing human-dev tooling (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus](sources/manus-context-engineering-lessons.md): first-party: Manus rebuilt its agent framework four times (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [What I learned building an opinionated and minimal coding agent](sources/mariozechner-pi-minimal-coding-agent.md): anecdote: build for context control; cost is maintaining provider abstraction and TUI (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Anthropic cracks down on unauthorized Claude usage by third-party harnesses](sources/venturebeat-anthropic-third-party-harness-crackdown.md): independent: platform risk, subscription access limited to official clients (Jan 2026) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Hosting the Agent SDK](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-hosting.md): first-party: even with the loop bought, the builder owns sandboxing, session storage, tenant isolation, scaling, observability (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Building effective agents](sources/anthropic-building-effective-agents.md): first-party: start with raw API calls; frameworks add abstraction that obscures prompts (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [microsoft/autogen repository](sources/github-microsoft-autogen-archive-notice.md): first-party: AutoGen archived with no fixes; framework churn risk (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [HN Cloudflare OS thread](sources/hn-cloudflare-os-thread.md): 'smells like lock-in' vs 'you can fork it'; open source but contingent on Cloudflare's PaaS (anecdote) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Vibe Kanban shutdown](sources/vibekanban-shutdown.md): dependency risk of adopting a small vendor's orchestration tool (first-party) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare OS rollout post](sources/cloudflare-how-we-rethink-work-with-cloudflare-os.md): second internal-platform build-then-open-source account (v1 May 2026, v2 open sourced 2026-08-05), self-reported (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Are Agent Harnesses the new "secret sauce" for Product Teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-harnesses-secret-sauce.md): Square's head of product calls context management and progressive tool disclosure "at the harness layer" Managerbot's secret sauce; harness as "agentic moat" (second-hand via VentureBeat) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build an AI Agent](sources/departmentofproduct-how-to-build-an-ai-agent.md): early three-way choice (framework / from scratch / no-code), from before "extend a vendor harness" was an option (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025](sources/mit-nanda-genai-divide-2025.md): counter-evidence: external partnerships reached deployment ~67% vs ~33% for internal builds; report says correlation, not causation (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## compounding-context-repo: Context that compounds with each shipped feature
A shared, agent-readable, harness-agnostic store of product context ("evidence, not yet fact", with domain owners), which every spec writes back to. This is the harness's memory layer.
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): monorepo World holds code, skills, conventions, intent documents, runbooks, AGENTS.md and zone knowledge; sessions leave "a pebble, a skill update, an AGENTS.md diff" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River's reaction to the Shop floor post](sources/x-tobi-river-reaction-to-shop-floor-post.md): "AGENTS.md files are mirror surfaces": writing them forces teams to find they "didn't quite agree with each other" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify's River: The AI Agent as Organizational Memory](sources/aienabledpm-shopify-river-organizational-memory.md): agent failures as context, permission and taste gaps, fixed by making knowledge explicit (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How to use Claude Code for non-engineering use cases](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-code-non-engineers.md): a PM's shared "Claude Code Product OS" repo of frameworks, strategy templates and stakeholder profiles (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to speed up engineering velocity with AI: a non-engineer's guide](sources/departmentofproduct-engineering-velocity-non-engineers.md): CLAUDE.md records code style, tests, repo etiquette and setup for new hires and the agent alike (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Why Atlassian Rovo Failed Us](sources/devto-tschimev-why-atlassian-rovo-failed-us.md): .cursorrules, skills/ directory and ADRs in the repo as the agent's context (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): a plain-text context repo, a domain owner per topic, spec write-back (Action 5) (research-product-agent-and-harness)
- [github/spec-kit (README)](sources/github-spec-kit-readme.md): state kept under .specify/ (memory, bugs/<slug>/, assessments/<slug>/ with decision.md). (user-story-mapping)
- [How Claude remembers your project (Claude Code docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-memory-docs.md): the hierarchy managed policy > user > project > local lets org, team and personal context layer. (user-story-mapping)

## cost-control-routing: Cost metering and model routing built into the harness
Open access to frontier models blew budgets; Ramp added per-project meters, limits and a router that picks the model.
- [Introducing Glass: Learn Things Once.](sources/x-eglyman-introducing-glass-learn-things-once.md): $1.5M week, taxi meter, Ramp Router, 30% drop claimed (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp: Lessons from Building a New AI Product - The Pragmatic Summit](sources/pragmatic-engineer-ramp-lessons-new-ai-product.md): LLM proxy with per-team cost tracing and config-only model swaps (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass. Make your entire company smarter](sources/ramp-introducing-glass.md): budget blown in weeks; users default to frontier models (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How to get your company AI pilled](sources/x-geoffintech-ai-pilled-article.md): the opposite stance in April: "Kill token limits and access restrictions", "treat AI usage as an infinite learning budget"; metering came later with Router/Glass (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp Router launch posts (Jul 20, 2026)](sources/x-ramp-router-launch-posts.md): the 30% bill cut is a Router claim from July 2026, 'without any performance degradation' (Zaks); no published data (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp built an AI agent harness in six weeks](sources/thenewstack-ramp-laminar-agent-harness.md): independent data point on in-harness routing, LangChain Open SWE -64% median cost/thread, no significant quality change (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): Ramp Router sits in the harness as the LLM gateway; model choice per cost/latency/performance (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building an agentic harness that outlasts the model](sources/shopify-engineering-agentic-harness-outlasts-model.md): full scan $50–300, diff scan $5–50; partitions sized to 20–30% of the context window (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): no token limits but "circuit breakers"; token leaderboard replaced by a usage dashboard where anyone sees their own spend (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How Shopify built an AI stack that doesn't care which models survive](sources/venturebeat-shopify-ai-stack-model-agnostic.md): the proxy auto-moved users to Opus or GPT 5.5 when "Claude Fable 5 shut down" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [From Memo to Movement](sources/firstround-shopify-ai-culture.md): in 2025 a token-spend leaderboard was "a cool proxy for value"; by 2026 it was removed (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): Kai projects set the default model and can block expensive models for a workflow (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Production-grade AI agents for financial compliance: Lessons from Stripe](sources/aws-stripe-compliance-agents.md): all LLM calls go through an LLM Proxy (noisy-neighbour limits, fallbacks, usage tracking by privacy class); prompt caching cut cost 60% (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Use Claude Code in the cloud (Claude Code on the web docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): no separate VM charge; cloud sessions share the account's rate limits, so parallel tasks consume limits proportionately (Limitations) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Automate work with scheduled tasks (Claude Code routines docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-scheduled-tasks.md): hourly caps (100 scheduled runs/hr per account, 30/hr per task for run-now and API fires) and subscription usage draw-down, no overage by default (Usage and limits) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [The $47K agent loop: why logging, monitoring and max_tokens all failed to stop it](sources/devto-47k-agent-loop.md): claims four LangChain agents on A2A looped (Verifier requesting, Analyzer producing) with no termination condition or budget cap; 'They had logging. They had monitoring. They did not have a hard limit.' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Durable Execution for AI Agents: LangGraph, DBOS, Inngest and Temporal Compared](sources/hackernoon-durable-execution-compared.md): payloads must stay in network rules out Inngest unless self-hosted (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How Ramp built a full-context background coding agent on Modal](sources/modal-ramp-inspect-background-agent.md): sessions start in seconds from a filesystem snapshot refreshed by a cron every 30 minutes (repos cloned, dependencies installed, build run); startup speed framed as the adoption driver (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Oz Cloud Agents & Orchestration (Warp docs)](sources/warp-oz-cloud-agents.md): runs incur platform plus compute plus inference charges; personal BYOK not supported for cloud runs; team-managed inference on Business/Enterprise (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Ramp Inspect Architecture 2026: How Background Coding Agents Scale Safely](sources/wavect-ramp-inspect-architecture.md): measure accepted changes per unit of review effort and incident risk, not PRs per day; review capacity and CI become the bottleneck (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Hosting the Agent SDK](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-hosting.md): first-party: token cost dominates container cost by an order of magnitude; per-session cost tracking available (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness design for long-running application development](sources/anthropic-harness-design-long-running-apps.md): first-party: 20x cost for the full harness on one task (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus](sources/manus-context-engineering-lessons.md): first-party: KV-cache hit rate is the key production metric (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Pi coding agent locked out](sources/yage-pi-coding-agent-locked-out.md): anecdote: Claude subscription credit works only in Claude Code, so other harnesses pay API rates (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Omnigent contextual policies](sources/databricks-omnigent-contextual-policies.md): soft/hard session cost caps that force a cheaper model; per-user daily caps (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare OS announcement](sources/cloudflare-os-announcement.md): all inference via AI Gateway with attribution and budgets per person/team/workspace (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare AI code review](sources/cloudflare-ai-code-review-opencode.md): $0.20 trivial to $1.68 full review by risk tier; shared context file prevents multiplying tokens (first-party) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Vaughan](sources/danielvaughan-meta-harness-pattern-pi.md): cross-harness delegation can multiply cost ~23-25x internal sessions (independent practitioner) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Warp Oz](sources/warp-oz-multi-harness.md): per-team billing and credit caps, but third-party harness inference bills outside Warp's summaries (vendor docs) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Decision Models Explained - The New AI Building Block for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-decision-models.md): routing steps (which tool, model or team) are usually a small LLM call returning one word; a typed-answer decision model does them faster and cheaper (Higgsfield auto-routing, Harvey Vault, both second-hand) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Perplexity's new Computer...](sources/departmentofproduct-perplexity-computer.md): each subtask is routed to a different vendor's model; credit-metered use means always-on workers need watching (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to develop a Headless Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-headless-product-strategy.md): Rippling claims a single code-mode MCP tool is 98% cheaper than chained tool calls (vendor claim) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to Manage AI Agents Effectively](sources/departmentofproduct-managing-ai-agents.md): three spend tactics (gateway budgets at Databricks and Vercel; routing by task difficulty, where Block's Buzz benchmark found the priciest model cost about 5.5x for about 9 points more quality; dedicated spend products from Ramp and Rippling, with Rippling's set against PR volume and rework). All second-hand. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use /loops, /goals and other Powerful Slash Commands as a Non-Engineer](sources/departmentofproduct-loops-goals-slash-commands.md): /compact pitched to PMs as a token-cost saver, with a steerable focus (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Productboard Plans & Pricing (Spark)](sources/productboard-pricing-spark.md): PM agent metered in credits per maker (500/mo Business; 1,500 + 800/maker Enterprise); top-ups $5/50 credits (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## docs-as-code-prd: PRDs and specs as files in the repo
Whether product specs live as markdown in git and how consistent that practice is.
- [Spec Kit and spec-driven.md (GitHub)](sources/github-spec-kit-sdd.md): spec is declared the source of truth ('Specifications don't serve code' is the doc's own framing); lives in git, one branch per feature. (user-story-mapping)
- [Specs (Kiro docs)](sources/kiro-specs-docs.md): specs are plain markdown files the agent keeps updated (task status); storage path not stated on the page fetched. (user-story-mapping)
- [Understanding Spec-Driven-Development: Kiro, spec-kit, and Tessl](sources/fowler-bockeler-sdd-kiro-speckit-tessl.md): three levels (spec-first, spec-anchored, spec-as-source); all tools are spec-first, few commit to spec-anchored; spec-kit creates a branch per spec so specs behave like change requests. (user-story-mapping)
- [MADR: Markdown Architectural Decision Records](sources/adr-madr-template.md): sections Context and Problem Statement, Decision Drivers, Considered Options, Decision Outcome (Consequences, Confirmation), Pros/Cons; versioned with code. (user-story-mapping)
- [Cursor is a much better product manager (Lenny's Newsletter)](sources/lenny-cursor-better-product-manager.md): blurb lists 'Why source-controlled markdown files might replace traditional SaaS tools' and a chapter on creating PRDs in Cursor with source control (anecdote; no detail). (user-story-mapping)

## enablement-by-product: The product is the enablement
Teach users by what the product does (suggested skills, memory, self-healing) rather than training.
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): principle 3; "every feature is secretly a lesson" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)

- [We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment](sources/shopify-engineering-remote-dev.md): adoption needed internal ads with a River persona; River went from 6% to 61% of merged mobile PRs (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Learning on the Shop floor](sources/x-tobi-learning-on-the-shop-floor.md): learning "does not require a curriculum, a training plan, or a manager. It just requires everyone's work to be visible" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Make the Work Visible](sources/airealized-make-the-work-visible.md): visibility as the adoption lever; peer practices (AI Corner, failure labs) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How Stripe Built Kai on Deep Agents (LangChain)](sources/langchain-how-stripe-built-kai-deep-agents.md): adoption came from removing knobs: users who bounced off configurable tools found Kai needed none (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): pilot with GTM (200-300 users), then a company-wide demo triggered the ramp (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Uber Agentic Pods (CTO post)](sources/x-praveen-uber-agentic-pods.md): 16 two-week pods in 16 functions: shadow, prioritise, build with the expert, validate, ship ('building with them, not for them') (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How Stripe Built a new Internal AI Knowledge Platform (Department of Product)](sources/departmentofproduct-stripe-kai.md): 'start with one domain and one surface', the most repeatable job in the tool people already use (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How to Build Powerful Internal AI Productivity Tools](sources/departmentofproduct-internal-ai-tools-ramp-glass.md): auto-connect at sign-on; "configuration already happened at the identity layer" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to speed up engineering velocity with AI: a non-engineer's guide](sources/departmentofproduct-engineering-velocity-non-engineers.md): Brex gives engineers a monthly tool budget and adopts company-wide whatever spreads (second-hand) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

The identity, audit, policy, data-retention and cost controls a harness gives an org admin, and on which surfaces they are enforced. It is the baseline a regulated owner compares any build or layer against.

(research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)

(research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)

- [Audit log events for agents (GitHub Copilot docs) and Reviewing audit logs for Copilot](sources/github-copilot-agentic-audit-log-events.md): Defines what a regulated org can evidence about agent actions on GitHub: each agent event carries `actor_is_agent`, the initiating `user` and an `agent_session_id`, retained 180 days and streamable to a SIEM. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
