## one-job-per-agent: One job per agent
Scoping an agent to one defined job (with human in the loop) for consistency and evals. In tension with [[single-agent-many-skills]].
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Stripe: 'keep agents specialized (on research, coding, or browser-native tools) while exposing them to capabilities in other systems' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [12-Factor Agents, factor 10](sources/humanlayer-12-factor-agents-small-focused-agents.md): first-party: small focused agents (about 3-10 steps) because LLMs lose focus as context grows; scope grows only as quality holds (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Measuring Agents in Production](sources/arxiv-measuring-agents-in-production.md): independent: 68% of deployed agents execute at most 10 steps before human intervention; reliability is the top challenge (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Orchestrating AI Code Review at scale](sources/cloudflare-ai-code-review-opencode.md): first-party: seven narrow specialist reviewers plus a coordinator beat one big prompt; 'what not to flag' per specialist (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Don't Build Multi-Agents](sources/cognition-dont-build-multi-agents.md): reconciliation note: its objection is to splitting interdependent work across parallel agents, not to bounded single-job agents (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Multi Agent Architecture explained](sources/departmentofproduct-multi-agent-architecture.md): the 2025 case for multi-agent: a single agent is "overwhelmed" by too many tools and too much context (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Turning Customer Feedback Noise into Actionable Insights (Azure AI Foundry blog)](sources/microsoft-feedback-noise-multi-agent.md): each specialist agent has its own schema, retrieval and guardrails. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The sweet spot for current-generation agentic AI (Vercel)](sources/vercel-sweet-spot-agentic-ai.md): lead triage went from a team of 10 to one person; abuse agent cut time to ticket closing 59% (baseline unstated); d0 'most used' is from SaaStr, not this post [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## opportunity-to-code-chain: Opportunity → problem → goal → intent → plan → code
A stage chain for product work, drawn by a Stripe engineer, in which agents today own the lower stages (intent research, plan, code, review) and people own the upper ones (opportunity, problem, goal) through customer conversations. It gives the strategy a spine: where each agent sits, where hand-offs and artifacts are, and where captured context must feed in.
- [An Inside Look Into How This $159B Tech Company Ships So Fast](sources/youtube-notmybusiness-inside-stripe-ships-fast.md): whiteboard at ~12:24 reads Opportunity → Problem → Goal → Intent → Plan, with a brace over Problem and Goal labelled (partly legible) "Customer conv…"; "This is the part that today is happening a lot more in Orbit now"; the plan is then handed to a minion to code (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): Geoff's eight-step Stripe/Ramp loop starts at informal intent and runs to staged release; Stripe's chain adds the three human stages above intent (opportunity, problem, goal) that the loop leaves implicit (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe's Internal Agent Ecosystem for Product Development](sources/claude-doc-geoff-stripe-internal-agent-ecosystem.md): Geoff's flow maps Kai (research), Harbor/Protodash (prototype), Orbit (plan), Minions (build), review agent plus human onto the same chain (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [AI didn't write our SDK. It changed how we built it.](sources/stripe-ai-didnt-write-our-sdk.md): between intent and code, agents draft specs that humans review as GitHub issues before implementation (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Intercom Fin NPI](sources/intercom-fin-npi-agent-readiness.md): adds a step after code: shipped work is written back into the agent's knowledge, tested, and monitored for 2-4 weeks (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [What are Claude Skills and how can you use them for product-related work?](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-skills-for-product-work.md): Notion's Spec to Implementation skill goes spec, plan page, 42 tracked tasks, then Claude Code status updates, but assumes the whole cycle lives in Notion (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Self-improving Product](sources/departmentofproduct-self-improving-product.md): signal → judge → spec (codebase-checked, complexity-tagged) → routed to Claude Code or Linear → review agent checks the PR against the spec's acceptance criteria and instrumentation (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): research → shortlist → PRD → screens → stakeholder PowerPoint, all in one Claude Code session over the Stitch MCP (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical Agent Skills for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-practical-agent-skills.md): compound-engineering splits brainstorm (what), plan (how) and work, with an artifact between each stage. Atlassian's official skill turns a Confluence spec into a Jira epic plus tickets and shows the breakdown for approval first (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

## org-context-grounding: Agents work when grounded in organisation context
Successful PM agents read the organisation's own data (docs, tickets, calls, code); thin context yields generic output. Related: [[compounding-context-repo]], [[harness-over-model]].
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): Kai knows the user and org chart by default, reads the project-management system, and connects Drive, Slack and DMs only if the user opts in (toggleable per session) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Emily Glassberg Sands on Latent Space](sources/latentspace-emily-sands-stripe.md): Hubert (text-to-SQL) failed most at data discovery; fixed by deprecating low-quality tables, owner-written docs, and org-position persona context (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How can we help everyone become a 10x engineer? (Stripe Sessions 2024)](sources/stripe-sessions-2024-10x-engineer-panel.md): Stripe put an LLM bot over Trailhead only after owners verified docs and the hierarchy was trusted, so answers 'were going to be accurate' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Decision Models Explained - The New AI Building Block for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-decision-models.md): in Rippling's GrowthOS test a classifier won on email triage (90% vs 50%) but failed as a text-to-SQL control step because it couldn't read business definitions like "qualified pipeline"; hybrid recommended (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents Explained - a simple overview of the basics](sources/departmentofproduct-context-engineering-basics.md): calendar-agent example; a rich reply needs contacts, calendar, past threads and send tools (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Claude Cowork as a Competitive Intelligence System](sources/departmentofproduct-cowork-competitive-intelligence.md): recommends a "my-company" folder of strategy decks and OKRs and a competitor list kept as a file so the agent can judge strategic gaps (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Claude Design is here](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-design.md): setup starts with a design system imported from a repo, code folder or .fig file. Claude extracts the components into an editable library (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Strategy Thought Partner](sources/departmentofproduct-strategy-thought-partner.md): a company-context settings page whose text feeds every analysis (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use AI to generate product requirements documents (Atticus Li)](sources/atticusli-ai-prd-generation.md): AI PRDs lack specificity; blamed mainly on missing context, partly on model habits (anecdotal) [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [ChatPRD AI review (Banani)](sources/banani-chatprd-ai-review.md): Competitor BuildBetter: ChatPRD has no customer-evidence layer; output depends on the context the PM supplies [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Ramp AI product factory: internal tools (BuildBetter blog)](sources/buildbetter-ramp-ai-product-factory.md): Glass connects Snowflake, research, strategy, spec format, codebase and design system (via summary). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Ramp's AI build factory: 75% of pull requests now written by agents (Dealroom summary of Geoff Charles talk)](sources/dealroom-ramp-ai-build-factory-summary.md): Glass value rests on a written spec format, principles and connected systems. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [We gave Claude Code to everyone at Intercom](sources/intercom-we-gave-claude-code-to-everyone.md): 'guidance skills' teach Claude company metrics and table mappings. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Cursor is a much better product manager (Lenny's Newsletter)](sources/lenny-cursor-better-product-manager.md): Codebase grounding of PRDs (Builder.io); 'prototypes generic/disconnected' claim unverified [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Meta VP's personal agents (Lenny's Newsletter write-up of The Skip Podcast)](sources/lenny-newsletter-meta-chawla-pm-leader-agents.md): analytics agent answers data questions in about five minutes using queries the data scientist already wrote; depends on Meta's habit of documenting experiments. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Roles aren't converging—they're expanding | Tamar Yehoshua (Atlassian CPO)](sources/lenny-podcast-tamar-yehoshua-roles-expanding.md): tools work because they see the org's context via Atlassian's "teamwork graph" (03:31, 16:33). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The bottleneck keeps shifting: what AI is changing about how we build (Gamma interview)](sources/atlassian-bottleneck-keeps-shifting-gamma.md): Documenting context for humans and agents is part of the PM's new bottleneck. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [CBTW on Rovo since launch](sources/cbtw-atlassian-rovo-real-world-feedback.md): Value depends on configuration, data quality and prompt design; out-of-the-box use feels "half baked" (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Why Atlassian Rovo Failed Us](sources/devto-tschimev-why-atlassian-rovo-failed-us.md): Replacement works, author says, because conventions, skills and ADRs live in the repo (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Atlassian Teamwork Graph: The context engine behind your AI (Atlassian blog)](sources/atlassian-blog-teamwork-graph-team-26.md): Atlassian says grounding responses in Teamwork Graph data gave "44% more accurate results" with "48% fewer tokens"; internal benchmark, no method (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Teamwork Graph glossary (Atlassian developer docs)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-glossary.md): ACLs are specified per object that a connector adds, so permissions travel with the object. (user-story-mapping)
- [What are projects? (Claude Help Center)](sources/anthropic-claude-projects-support.md): uploaded knowledge is the grounding, switching to RAG on paid plans when nearing context limits (up to 10x capacity per the page). (user-story-mapping)
- [Organize work with projects (Claude Cowork docs)](sources/anthropic-cowork-projects-docs.md): Project holds: description (Dispatch reads it to choose a project for a task), folders (one or more local), instructions, links, linked Chat projects, memory. (user-story-mapping)
- [Glean Enterprise Graph (product page)](sources/glean-enterprise-graph-product-page.md): graph of high-value entities (projects, people, customers, products) linked to docs, tickets and specs; permissions-enforced via connectors. (user-story-mapping)

## org-learning-loop: One person's win becomes everyone's baseline
Skills, prompts and corrections made by one employee propagate to the team so the organisation learns once. Overlaps with [[compounding-context-repo]] (product context) but is about workflow/skills and shared sessions.
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): principle 2 and Dojo, 350+ skills (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass: Learn Things Once.](sources/x-eglyman-introducing-glass-learn-things-once.md): 323 employees, 6,500+ edits to what Glass knows; Finance taught it the UK-customer rule (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass. Make your entire company smarter](sources/ramp-introducing-glass.md): shareable sessions, 0:48-1:01 (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How to get your company AI pilled](sources/x-geoffintech-ai-pilled-article.md): L0-L3 ladder, leaderboards, center + spokes (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Inside Ramp's Custom Agent Operating System](sources/notion-inside-ramps-custom-agent-os.md): pre-Glass layer; sales feedback piped into Notion and triaged to the roadmap by agents (0:40-1:20) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Eric Glyman April 2026 posts on Glass and AI adoption](sources/x-eglyman-april-glass-posts.md): "when one person on a team figures out a better workflow, everyone on that team gets it" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Today, we're launching Glass (Geoff Charles X post)](sources/x-geoffintech-glass-launch.md): "Adoption, it turns out, is the easy part. The hard part is making AI work compound." (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass (Ramp X post)](sources/x-tryramp-introducing-glass.md): tagline contrasts individual speed with company-level learning (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Other Ramp (@tryramp) posts about Glass, Apr-May 2026](sources/x-tryramp-other-glass-posts.md): company-account amplification; Ramptables episode on the Glass builders (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Learning on the Shop floor](sources/x-tobi-learning-on-the-shop-floor.md): River refuses DMs so others learn by watching (Lehrwerkstatt); a checkout-warehouse skill reused by 12 teams; merge rate 36%→77% credited to people writing down what River should have known (self-reported) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tobi's replies about River](sources/x-tobi-river-replies-may-2026.md): "It's not about the transcript of the work. It's about seeing how other people begin the work with the ai" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): the public transcript corpus is mined and fed back into skills, prompts and defaults; "the privacy of an agent thread is a disadvantage" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tobi Lütke: AI Agents, Better Decisions (Knowledge Project)](sources/fs-knowledge-project-tobi-lutke-ai-agents.md): open channels only, to recreate office "osmosis learning"; "a late choice ... one of my favorite calls" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment](sources/shopify-engineering-remote-dev.md): the cheap "Jev" classifier tags every mobile River thread, scores outcomes, and failures feed an LLM to improve River (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Learning on the Shop floor (Simon Willison)](sources/simonwillison-learning-on-the-shop-floor.md): compares River to Midjourney's public-Discord interface as a way to learn a finicky new skill (independent opinion) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [The Transparency Paradox (Bernstein)](sources/asq-bernstein-transparency-paradox.md): counter-evidence: broad visibility bred hiding; curtained lines +10–15% output; learning shared upward once there was data (independent, factory 2009) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify River (Ashgaliyev wiki)](sources/ashgaliyev-wiki-shopify-river.md): River as "organizational apprenticeship" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River: Shopify's Slack-native AI agent (video)](sources/youtube-shopify-river-slack-native-agent.md): official one-line positioning is the public-only constraint (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): roadmap: Kai reflects on traces involving a skill, proposes and tests improvements, submits them for the skill owner's review (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe's payment method factory](sources/stripe-payment-method-factory.md): learning logs, decision logs, transcripts and PR comments from each run feed an agent that proposes updates to 100+ reusable prompts; an observer agent hardens prompts (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [The AI Agent Doom Loop: Why Your Agent Keeps Making the Same Mistake](sources/unblocked-agent-doom-loop.md): a correction made in one session does not reach the next; Unblocked sells the fix (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent skills at enterprise scale](sources/paypal-agent-skills-at-enterprise-scale.md): thousands of employees; per-function/persona plugin bundles planned. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
