- [Don't Use Generative AI to Replace Discovery with Real Humans](sources/producttalk-generative-ai-discovery.md): use AI on surveys, NPS, tickets and analytics, with the human guiding and checking (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Building My First AI Product: 6 Lessons from My 90-Day Deep Dive](sources/producttalk-ai-playbook-first-ai-product.md): on two transcripts Claude found 18/20 opportunities vs her 15/19, added 8/2 she missed, missed 7 of hers each time (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How AI will impact product management](sources/lenny-how-ai-will-impact-product-management.md): discovery 3/5: AI finds signal in customer data, but customers still want people (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Customer Interview Analysis: Where AI Helps and Hurts](sources/producttalk-customer-interview-analysis-ai.md): Torres synthesises first, then uses AI as a fresh perspective that sometimes catches what she missed (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Build on Dovetail (docs)](sources/dovetail-build-on-dovetail.md): MCP can read workspace content and create projects, docs, data, highlights and channel data. (user-story-mapping)

## risk-review-as-classification: Risk review as a specification and classification problem
Risk advisory works as classification against a known taxonomy, with a curation path for novel risks. That makes a risk agent tractable to build and straightforward to evaluate with SME labels.
- [Decision Models Explained - The New AI Building Block for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-decision-models.md): the same "is this safe to run?" check before every agent action, where speed matters; Vercel's CEO is relayed as claiming 18x faster safety checks (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Intent Shaping in a Well-Managed Environment](sources/geoff-intent-shaping-well-managed-environment.md): a MECE taxonomy, component-by-risk scoring, false positives and negatives as heuristic fixes (§Risk review as classification; §Evaluation) (research-product-agent-and-harness)

## risk-sloped-review: Human review sloped to risk
How much human review agent output gets depends on how risky it is. Where that line sits is a key harness and governance design choice, especially in regulated organisations.
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): "Hand off the decision, not the investigation"; River recommended dropping its own patch when a developer surfaced the original requirement (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Are Agent Harnesses the new "secret sauce" for Product Teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-harnesses-secret-sauce.md): split actions by reversibility: easy-to-undo actions in the agent's free zone, payments, publishing and financial records in a hardcoded layer (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to Identify Opportunities for AI Automation](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-automation-opportunities.md): cost-if-wrong is an explicit axis, colour-coded on the canvas; drafting legal terms fails even though it is verifiable, because it is high-risk and infrequent. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): Ramp auto-approves low-complexity PRs; Stripe requires human review on every change (§Vision, step 7) (research-product-agent-and-harness)

## scoped-governance-containers: Governance scoped to a project or workspace
Policy (default model, allowed tools, human-in-the-loop rules, data back end, even which harness) set once by a project owner and applied to everyone working in that project, rather than per user or org-wide. Matters for governance and trust defaults.
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): "projects are primarily a governance mechanism"; owners set default model, tool policies, HITL; HR has a separately backed secure project; projects of 5 to 500 people (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): domain-owned custom Kai agents load a team's skills and data sources by default (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)

## shared-persistent-sessions: Shared, persistent, multi-user agent sessions
Agent sessions that outlive one person's laptop: shared with teammates, running in a deployed runtime, resumable or event-driven. Raises identity (who is the agent acting as), permission-leakage, durability and cost questions that local sessions avoid.
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): async-by-default, always-open sessions with HITL approvals, steering and multiplayer; session state in Postgres decoupled from sandboxes; cloud workers so 'laptop goes to sleep' no longer matters (first-party) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): Aquifer session = append-only Postgres event log; harness and sandbox disposable; idle "session cells" rehydrate on any host; "Cells die, sandboxes die, machines die. The conversation doesn't." (Part III) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River floods Shopify chart](sources/x-tobi-river-floods-shopify-chart.md): "wrote in the same thread" links 61,680 (Mar) → 171,853 (Sep 2026), the only published multiplayer metric (self-reported) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment](sources/shopify-engineering-remote-dev.md): each River session claims a warm Mac plus Android VM, destroyed after use; tasks start from Slack or run overnight; Live Preview links shareable (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify: Building River (ZenML)](sources/zenml-llmops-shopify-river-durable-infrastructure.md): Postgres event-log session, harness outside the sandbox, idle "session cells" restart anywhere (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Case Study: Shopify River (Wallfacer)](sources/wallfacer-case-study-shopify-river.md): "the resume mechanism and the audit record are the same artifact" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Hacker News: River submissions and comments](sources/hn-shopify-river-discussion.md): practitioners compare River to Managed Agents and say "we built something similar" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): Kai sessions are cloud-hosted and long (one hit 932 turns) but single-user; context is 'locked in'; sharing and multi-person artifacts are on the roadmap (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe's AI minions ship 1,300 PRs weekly from a Slack emoji (How I AI)](sources/howiai-stripe-minions-kaliski.md): minions run in a public Slack 'robots' channel watched by 76 people: open-by-default observation and 'pair prompting' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Harbor shares artifacts, not sessions: one published snapshot per URL, anchored comments that re-resolve after agent rewrites, remix into a copy (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Thoughts On A Month With Devin](sources/answerai-month-with-devin.md): the Slack-based chat and visible environment setup were polished; the unreliability was in the agent (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Use Claude Code in the cloud (Claude Code on the web docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): cloud sessions keep running after the laptop closes and can be steered from mobile; sharing is Private or Team visibility, and 'recipients see the latest state when they open the link, but their view doesn't update in real time' (Share sessions) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Automate work with scheduled tasks (Claude Code routines docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-scheduled-tasks.md): scheduled tasks 'belong to your individual claude.ai account. They are not shared with teammates'; everything they do through GitHub/connectors 'appears as you' (Create a scheduled task) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Tag: agent identity (concepts)](sources/anthropic-claude-tag-agent-identity.md): channel sessions use connectors, repos and plugins an admin applied to the channel/workspace/org, and 'everyone in the channel gets the same capability, regardless of who asks' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): first design ran session, harness and sandbox in one container, making it a 'pet'; decoupling into session (durable log), harness (loop) and sandbox (hands) lets any piece fail or be replaced (Decoupling) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Self-hosted environments (Claude Code cloud sessions on your infrastructure)](sources/anthropic-self-hosted-environments.md): control plane (queue, session stream, claude.ai UI) stays Anthropic-hosted; runners execute sessions; 'Anthropic stores the session transcript so you can resume the session from another supported surface' (What stays on your infrastructure) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Self-hosted environments (Claude Code cloud sessions on your infrastructure)](sources/anthropic-self-hosted-environments.md): a runner locks to one owner (a user account or a Claude Tag agent) at a time so checked-out code never mixes between owners; minimum fleet size equals active owners (Runner lifecycle) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Long-running agents (Cloudflare Agents SDK docs)](sources/cloudflare-agents-long-running-agents.md): agents are 'durable identities, not always-on processes': wake on HTTP, WebSocket, RPC, alarm or inbound email, hibernate after about 2 minutes idle; eviction can occur at any point (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloud-origin agents have no 'Move to Machine' option (Cursor forum)](sources/cursor-forum-cloud-to-local-handoff.md): related thread reports local to cloud handoff failing for GitLab repos with 'Background composer not found' (search snippet only) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cursor Cloud Agent sessions are shared across users - act on behalf (forum bug report)](sources/cursor-forum-team-followups-act-on-behalf.md): the reporter claims a session runs with the initiating user's OAuth identity for Jira, GitHub and Slack while its prompt surface is not bound to that user; follow-ups via Slack thread or the shared web URL run as the initiator (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [The $47K agent loop: why logging, monitoring and max_tokens all failed to stop it](sources/devto-47k-agent-loop.md): argues enforcement should be deterministic, pre-call and per-run (cost, iterations, wall clock) with an external kill switch, separate from the agent (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent](sources/github-copilot-cloud-agent-risks.md): identity: commits are authored by Copilot with the requesting developer as co-author, signed ('Verified'), each linked to its session log; logs and audit events available to admins (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent](sources/github-copilot-cloud-agent-risks.md): only users with write access can trigger the agent and comments from others never reach it; pushes confined to one branch (the PR branch or a new copilot/ branch) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Open-Inspect (ColeMurray/background-agents) README](sources/github-open-inspect-background-agents.md): a Durable Object per session holds SQLite, a WebSocket hub and event stream; clients are web, Slack, GitHub, Linear, webhooks; presence indicators and prompts attributed to authors in git commits (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Open-Inspect (ColeMurray/background-agents) README](sources/github-open-inspect-background-agents.md): access model has Workspace/Team/Private visibility separate from ownership, break-glass audited read for workspace owners, but 'Team-visibility read restrictions only apply when TEAMS_ENFORCEMENT=on. The default is shadow' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Durable Execution for AI Agents: LangGraph, DBOS, Inngest and Temporal Compared](sources/hackernoon-durable-execution-compared.md): 'None of the four saves a model call made outside a step boundary' so retries pay again; durability does not guarantee idempotency (a step that charged a card and timed out still needs handling) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [LangGraph persistence (checkpointers, threads, stores)](sources/langchain-langgraph-persistence.md): InMemory saver is for dev only; production uses Postgres/Sqlite savers; Agent Server handles persistence automatically; checkpoints accumulate over long conversations and need pruning (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How Ramp built a full-context background coding agent on Modal](sources/modal-ramp-inspect-background-agent.md): each session gets its own Modal sandbox; Modal Dicts hold session locks, Modal Queues route prompts from any client into the right session so several clients feed one session without conflict (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex cloud and the Slack integration (OpenAI docs)](sources/openai-codex-cloud-slack.md): repository work 'runs as a separate task under the requester's account'; a different account may start a new task instead of continuing; sharing an environment does not grant repo access or share credential values (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex cloud and the Slack integration (OpenAI docs)](sources/openai-codex-cloud-slack.md): approval requests go to the requester as a private card, but the response 'can be read by people with access to that channel'; following the channel reply does not give access to the task (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot, end-to-end coding agents - Part 2](sources/stripe-minions-part-2.md): blast radius bounded by environment not by prompts: devboxes (EC2, pre-warmed, ~10 s) run in QA with no real user data, production services or arbitrary egress; engineers run about half a dozen at once (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Production-ready agents with the OpenAI Agents SDK + Temporal](sources/temporal-openai-agents-sdk-integration.md): long-running tasks that crash resume where they left off because activity results and workflow progress are stored; claimed to save compute and token costs (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Tag Slack access model (Tenable Research)](sources/tenable-claude-tag-slack-access-model.md): service-identity pattern means 'anyone in a channel with the bundle can direct Claude within its scope'; public-channel join policy effectively governs access to bundle credentials; new members also see prior scrollback (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Trace (Thoughtworks Technology Radar Vol. 34)](sources/thoughtworks-radar-agent-trace.md): Radar ring: Assess; support cited in Cline, OpenCode and a Git AI implementation (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Oz Cloud Agents & Orchestration (Warp docs)](sources/warp-oz-cloud-agents.md): cloud run transcripts open in session sharing; a teammate can attach to a running task to monitor or steer it; Runs pages show status, trigger, creator and credit usage (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Ramp Inspect Architecture 2026: How Background Coding Agents Scale Safely](sources/wavect-ramp-inspect-architecture.md): blast radius is set by credentials, network egress, data, GitHub permissions, internal system access and auditability, not by the sandbox; scaling sandboxes without those controls yields 'hundreds of isolated ways to make a bad decision faster' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare OS announcement](sources/cloudflare-os-announcement.md): persistent per-employee workspaces; apps shareable live or as code-only blueprints; observation log re-checks a viewer's access to what the agent has seen (vendor claim, 2026-08-05) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare OS rollout post](sources/cloudflare-how-we-rethink-work-with-cloudflare-os.md): self-reported thousands of weekly users, >4,000 apps in 30 days, no measurement method (first-party, unverified) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [HN Cloudflare OS thread](sources/hn-cloudflare-os-thread.md): deployment reports (provider setup trouble, Workers Paid requirement) and doubts that per-user copies are maintainable (anecdote) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Project Think](sources/cloudflare-project-think.md): durable fibers, tree-structured sessions, DO sub-agents; frames laptop agents as lacking durability (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Omnigent repo](sources/github-omnigent-repo.md): shared sessions by URL, attach/fork; open issues on sharing/host-access separation and stuck-running sessions (first-party, 2026-10-23) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Sandbox survey](sources/rywalker-ai-agent-sandboxes.md): persistence differs by vendor (files vs memory vs processes); restoring a checkpoint does not undo external effects (independent, disclosed conflict) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Nx Polygraph](sources/nx-polygraph-meta-harness.md): session graph, resume by anyone with any agent (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Notion MCP supported tools](sources/notion-mcp-supported-tools.md): notion-spawn-session, wait-session, send-message-to-session, read-session-event let an outside agent start and observe Custom Agent sessions. (user-story-mapping)
- [Linear for Agents (developer docs)](sources/linear-developers-agents.md): agent sessions start automatically on mention or delegation; webhook expects a thought activity within 10 seconds. (user-story-mapping)
- [What are projects? (Claude Help Center)](sources/anthropic-claude-projects-support.md): 'Can view' vs 'Can edit' sharing for Team/Enterprise. (user-story-mapping)
- [Organize work with projects (Claude Cowork docs)](sources/anthropic-cowork-projects-docs.md): projects live on the computer only, not synced or shared; claude.ai projects are shareable on Team/Enterprise and can be linked, not merged. (user-story-mapping)
- [Why We Built Our Own Background Agent (Ramp Builders)](sources/ramp-builders-why-we-built-our-own-background-agent.md): 'Send your session to any colleague, and they can help take it home.'; each session has its own SQLite database; PRs are opened with the user's GitHub token so authors cannot self-approve agent changes. (user-story-mapping)

## single-agent-many-skills: One agent with many skills, not many agents
Consolidate to one agent and one conversational surface, extended by skills and tools.
- [Ramp: Lessons from Building a New AI Product - The Pragmatic Summit](sources/pragmatic-engineer-ramp-lessons-new-ai-product.md): "single agent with a thousand skills"; OmniChat (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass. Make your entire company smarter](sources/ramp-introducing-glass.md): "one single agent" with pre-built connectivity (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): new agents are "profiles" (prompt, skills, extensions, sandbox policy, model defaults) on one substrate: "a new bundle, not ... a new platform" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify Just Showed the Agent Stack](sources/adaptordie-shopify-river-agent-stack.md): "Pi is the engine room. River is the shop floor interface" (commentator's inference) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): one Kai harness over 1,000+ skills and tools; a no-code builder that produced 4,000+ micro-agents was replaced because of duplicated, uneven, hard-to-maintain agents (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How Stripe Built Kai on Deep Agents (LangChain)](sources/langchain-how-stripe-built-kai-deep-agents.md): skills gate tools via allowedTools (two-pass); foundational skills pinned; frontier-model quality degrades past ~150 skills with the system prompt (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): ~2,000 skills: ~50 used heavily daily, 100-150 by sub-orgs, many by 2-3 people; telemetry pipeline decides what to promote or move out of the general context (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot, end-to-end coding agents - Part 2](sources/stripe-minions-part-2.md): 'Toolshed' internal MCP server with nearly 500 tools but a small curated subset per agent; blueprints mix deterministic nodes with agent nodes (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Don't Build Multi-Agents](sources/cognition-dont-build-multi-agents.md): first-party: parallel sub-agents make conflicting implicit decisions; share full traces, prefer a single-threaded agent (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Skills specification](sources/agentskills-specification.md): progressive disclosure keeps many skills cheap. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Equipping agents with Agent Skills](sources/anthropic-engineering-equipping-agents-agent-skills.md): general agent plus loadable expertise. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [SkillsBench](sources/arxiv-skillsbench.md): 2-3 skills best; 4+ gives smaller gains (independent). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AGENTS.md outperforms skills](sources/vercel-agents-md-outperforms-skills.md): counter-evidence: on-demand skills unreliable for always-needed reference knowledge (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [Custom subagents in Claude Code](sources/anthropic-claude-code-subagents-docs.md): skills preloaded into subagents (up to 32). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex vs Claude Code multi-agent](sources/danielvaughan-codex-vs-claude-code-multi-agent.md): subagent topologies differ (anecdote). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Best practices for Claude Code](sources/anthropic-claude-code-best-practices.md): first-party: one general harness spans exploration (vague prompts) to unattended runs (claude -p, hooks, skills); skills for repeatable workflows (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Equipping agents with Agent Skills](sources/anthropic-engineering-equipping-agents-agent-skills.md): first-party: skills proposed instead of fragmented custom agents per use case (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How we built our multi-agent research system](sources/anthropic-multi-agent-research-system.md): first-party: multi-agent fits breadth-first research, not shared-context coding; about 15x tokens (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Choose a design pattern for your agentic AI system](sources/google-cloud-choose-design-pattern-agentic-ai.md): vendor: start with a single agent; go multi-agent when tool count or distinct responsibilities cause failures (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Why Semantic Data Layers matter](sources/departmentofproduct-semantic-data-layers.md): Anthropic pairs a thin "router" knowledge skill (semantic layer first, then domain files) with an analyst-workflow skill that ends in adversarial review. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

## skill-standards: Skill standards

- [Extend Claude with skills (Claude Code docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-skills-docs.md): skills and commands merged; `context: fork` runs a skill as a subagent (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Build skills (ChatGPT and Codex docs)](sources/openai-codex-skills-docs.md): Codex follows the open standard; 2% context budget for the skill list; "prefer instructions over scripts" (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AGENTS.md](sources/agentsmd-agents-md.md): schema-free repo instruction file, nearest file wins; 60k+ repos claimed (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Linux Foundation: Agentic AI Foundation](sources/linuxfoundation-agentic-ai-foundation.md): MCP, goose and AGENTS.md under neutral governance since 2025-12-09; SKILL.md governance not confirmed (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AGENTS.md outperforms skills in our agent evals](sources/vercel-agents-md-outperforms-skills.md): skill never invoked in 56% of cases; 53% baseline = 53% default skill; 79% with instruction; 100% AGENTS.md index (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [SkillsBench](sources/arxiv-skillsbench.md): curated skills +16.2pp avg but 16 of 84 tasks worse; self-generated -1.3pp; 2-3 skills best (independent). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Evaluating AGENTS.md](sources/arxiv-evaluating-agents-md.md): context files reduced success and raised cost 20%+ (independent). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Skills Open Standard: portable SKILL.md](sources/danielvaughan-agent-skills-open-standard-portable.md): no backward-compatibility guarantees or formal versioning (anecdote). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [About agent skills (GitHub Copilot docs)](sources/github-copilot-agent-skills-docs.md): Copilot reads .github/.claude/.agents skills; org-level skills not covered (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Gemini CLI and OpenCode skills support](sources/gemini-cli-and-opencode-skills-support.md): same SKILL.md; unknown frontmatter ignored (first-party via search summaries). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Test plugins with evals](sources/anthropic-claude-code-plugin-evals.md): skill-triggering failure is the common first finding (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [What are Claude Skills and how can you use them for product-related work?](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-skills-for-product-work.md): PM primer on the three SKILL.md layers and progressive disclosure; vendor skill zips ship with evals, examples and references folders (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to develop a Headless Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-headless-product-strategy.md): a tool is something an agent calls; a skill is something it reads (Webflow skills for Codex and ChatGPT) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical ways to use Claude Routines at work - a Guide for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-routines-for-product-teams.md): process in SKILL.md and voice in a separate brand file, reused by every routine that writes customer-facing text (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical Agent Skills for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-practical-agent-skills.md): recaps SKILL.md as three layers (a header for selection, the instructions, and files loaded only when needed). Skills load automatically, with no explicit call (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Notion MCP supported tools](sources/notion-mcp-supported-tools.md): tools to convert a page to a Skill, upload/download Skills; enabled-skill lists capped at 30; uploads up to 20 MiB compressed / 1,000 files. (user-story-mapping)

- [MalSkills](sources/arxiv-malskills.md): 400 confirmed malicious of 150,108 skills across 7 registries (independent). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [Agent skills at enterprise scale](sources/paypal-agent-skills-at-enterprise-scale.md): "Decentralize authoring. Centralize trust, governance, and distribution"; fail-closed validation + human review; no metrics (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Building plugins (Cursor docs)](sources/cursor-plugins-building.md): Cursor marketplace and team variables. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [How to use Cursor for Non-Engineering use cases](sources/departmentofproduct-cursor-for-non-engineers.md): Cursor's Plugin Marketplace bundles MCP, skills, agents and hooks into one-click installs (Feb 2026). (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

The post itself works as a hand-curated catalogue of 10 (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

## spec-becomes-prototype-and-evals: The spec is replaced by prototype plus evals
Some teams swap the PRD for a problem statement, a working prototype and evals.
- [AI didn't write our SDK. It changed how we built it.](sources/stripe-ai-didnt-write-our-sdk.md): a two-day prototype moved a scope decision weeks earlier; agents draft specs reviewed as GitHub issues before implementation (~20 lint rules) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Protodash (How I AI, Owen Williams)](sources/howiai-stripe-protodash-owen-williams.md): engineers worked from a designer's prototype PR: 'just use the prototype as the source of truth' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): the PRD is an intermediate step the agent writes; the screens are what goes to stakeholders (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Product development in the agentic era](sources/anthropic-product-development-agentic-era.md): specs live less in docs and more in working prototypes against pre-production API specs. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Meta VP's personal agents (Lenny's Newsletter write-up of The Skip Podcast)](sources/lenny-newsletter-meta-chawla-pm-leader-agents.md): for ML work the PRD was replaced by a one-paragraph problem statement plus prototype plus eval set. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [github/spec-kit (README)](sources/github-spec-kit-readme.md): Workflow: /speckit-constitution (once per project), then per feature /speckit-specify, -plan, -tasks, -implement, -converge. Runs as skills in the agent's chat. (user-story-mapping)
- [Spec-Driven Development (spec-kit spec-driven.md)](sources/github-spec-kit-spec-driven.md): contrast; here the spec stays primary and code is regenerated. (user-story-mapping)

Using agents to map edge cases and gaps in specs and designs before build.

- [What is a Command Line Interface and why do they suddenly matter to product teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-cli-for-product-teams.md): "Prepare me for my day" over calendar and inbox; one post-sprint-review instruction chains four Workspace CLI operations (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Claude Projects and Skills to Monitor your Product's Health](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-projects-product-health.md): a master Project writes an exec health report under 500 words with talking points (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

- [Practical ways to use MCP at work](sources/departmentofproduct-mcp-at-work.md): "chief of staff" daily briefing from calendar, Linear, Zendesk, Slack and news (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

- [How to use Claude Cowork as a Competitive Intelligence System](sources/departmentofproduct-cowork-competitive-intelligence.md): /stakeholder-update asks the update type and audience, then rewrites a research deck as a Slack-ready exec message (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to do AI-powered product discovery sprints](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-discovery-sprints.md): OpenAI's in-house assistant reportedly summarises research sessions and pushes insights to stakeholders in Slack (second-hand) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Product development in the agentic era](sources/anthropic-product-development-agentic-era.md): agents for adoption analytics with persistent database and memory replace manual reporting. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Ramp's AI build factory: 75% of pull requests now written by agents (Dealroom summary of Geoff Charles talk)](sources/dealroom-ramp-ai-build-factory-summary.md): 85% of PM-directed questions fully answered by AI (speaker-reported, via summary). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

(research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

(research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## svpg-four-risks: SVPG's four risks and role ownership
Cagan's value, usability, feasibility and viability risks and who owns each; a frame for which risks an agent can reduce.
- [Inside Atlassian's State of Product 2026: key takeaways](sources/mindtheproduct-atlassian-state-of-product-2026-takeaways.md): The 80% figure is used in the map as evidence that feasibility input arrives late (product trio collaboration is thin). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The Four Big Risks](sources/svpg-four-big-risks.md): Discovery addresses value, usability, feasibility and business viability risk; PM owns value and viability, designer usability, lead engineer feasibility. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## synthetic-users-limits: Synthetic users and AI personas: limits
AI-simulated research participants are optimistic, shallow and uncritical; supplement, never replace, real users.
- [How to build a Persona Feature Tester with Claude Code and ElevenLabs](sources/departmentofproduct-persona-feature-tester.md): personas billed as "grounded in real world data" but built from mock data that Cowork generated; no check against real users (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Strategy Thought Partner](sources/departmentofproduct-strategy-thought-partner.md): the base app runs features past "data-grounded" synthetic personas, including voice calls, with no validation discussed (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to do AI-powered product discovery sprints](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-discovery-sprints.md): Askable reportedly builds a queryable model from real interviews to answer hypothetical market questions, presented with no caveat (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Synthetic Replacements for Human Survey Data? The Perils of Large Language Models (Bisbee et al.)](sources/bisbee-synthetic-replacements-survey-data.md): persona-prompted LLM respondents show reduced variance and different regression estimates vs real respondents. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Synthetic Users: If, When, and How to Use AI-Generated 'Research'](sources/nngroup-synthetic-users.md): optimism bias, no priorities, uncritical concept approval; supplement but never replace real users. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Sycophantic AI decreases prosocial intentions and promotes dependence](sources/stanford-cheng-sycophantic-ai-science-2026.md): users rated sycophantic answers higher and trusted them more (2,405 participants; abstract via search) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## tacit-knowledge-capture: Capturing tacit knowledge from people for agents
How know-how that lives in people's heads (how the business works, which data to trust, design and architectural judgment) gets written down, verified and kept current so agents can use it: by passive mining of work exhaust, by experts curating docs, rules and skills, by interview-style elicitation, or by write-back from finished work. Bears on Geoff's hypothesis that a context-creation agent is needed.
- [How can we help everyone become a 10x engineer? (Stripe Sessions 2024)](sources/stripe-sessions-2024-10x-engineer-panel.md): Trailhead makes owners verify docs or they 'drift away and get archived'; the docs complaint dropped steeply in the next engineering survey (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [An Inside Look Into How This $159B Tech Company Ships So Fast](sources/youtube-notmybusiness-inside-stripe-ships-fast.md): a 2013 Stripe engineer: once 'no one has all of the state in their heads anymore' Stripe wrote documents, then robots, and now AI 'can ingest all of this documentation that we'd written' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Protodash (How I AI, Owen Williams)](sources/howiai-stripe-protodash-owen-williams.md): a design manager encoded design-system judgment as agent rules over 18 months: 'I feel insane writing these rules, but ... once you've got them, it works' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [AI didn't write our SDK. It changed how we built it.](sources/stripe-ai-didnt-write-our-sdk.md): repo-local docs 'written for AI consumption' (principles, boundaries, anti-patterns) raised agent output and cut onboarding for humans (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Inside Stripe's Engineering Culture: Part 2](sources/pragmaticengineer-inside-stripe-engineering-culture-part-2.md): CEO- and CTO-led internal writing culture; 'vastly more people consume the writing than produce it' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Investing in Internal Documentation (First Round, David Nunez)](sources/firstround-nunez-internal-documentation.md): knowledge 'trapped in an early hire's head'; internal docs lose to external docs and to the to-do list unless built into career expectations (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe's payment method factory](sources/stripe-payment-method-factory.md): planning agent interviews the engineer for context and writes it to a shared knowledge base; learning and decision logs feed prompt updates (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Latent Space, Emily Sands](sources/latentspace-emily-sands-stripe.md): canonical-dataset docs written by domain owners ('brute-forcing it with humans'); Sands did not yet trust an LLM to write them (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Agentic memory in Copilot](sources/github-blog-agentic-memory-copilot.md): write-back with verification: agents store memories with code citations, re-checked on read; A/B merge rate 83% to 90% (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [InterviewBot: LLM-led interviews](sources/arxiv-interviewbot-mllm-led-interviews.md): against interview agents as-is: LLM interviewers are 'acknowledgment-heavy but probe-light', 4.9% deepening probes in 428 turns (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Anthropic Interviewer](sources/anthropic-interviewer-launch.md): 1,250 AI-led interviews, 97.6% satisfied: scalable and liked, but it captures attitudes, not expertise (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Knowledge elicitation automation with LLMs](sources/swj-knowledge-elicitation-automation-llms.md): AI interviews were more efficient, but AI-built ontologies missed data and hallucinated (independent, weak) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Generative AI and the SECI model](sources/arxiv-uchihira-genai-seci-model.md): GenAI work on tacit knowledge is still 'fragmentary'; most GenAI KM handles explicit knowledge (independent position paper) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Scaling expertise with generative AI](sources/tandf-osullivan-scaling-expertise-genai.md): governance that needs persistent state can't be done by prompting alone; GenAI drifts and flatters (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Knowledge activation with curated skills](sources/arxiv-yahoo-knowledge-activation-skills.md): 87 curated skills saved 2.6 h/week; contribution barriers, authoring cost and unmeasured staleness (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [AI-generated table documentation](sources/databricks-ai-generated-table-documentation.md): agent drafts, owner accepts or edits: '>80%' of metadata updates AI-assisted (vendor claim) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Generative AI at Work](sources/nber-brynjolfsson-generative-ai-at-work.md): an assistant trained on top performers' work exhaust raised productivity 14% overall, 34% for novices, about 0 for experts (independent, causal) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [LLMs reduce public knowledge sharing](sources/pnas-nexus-llms-reduce-public-knowledge-sharing.md): Stack Overflow posting fell ~25% within six months of ChatGPT: people stop writing knowledge down once they can ask an AI (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Knowledge hiding meta-analysis](sources/ebr-knowledge-hiding-meta-analysis.md): 131 studies, 47,348 people: knowledge hiding is distinct from (uncorrelated with) sharing, so easier sharing won't fix it (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Copilot and works councils (Microsoft Inside Track)](sources/microsoft-insidetrack-copilot-works-councils.md): works councils objected to features that rank or monitor employees; staged rollout (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Resolution extraction from Slack vs tickets](sources/neurips-2025-resolution-extraction-slack-vs-tickets.md): knowledge mined from Slack is more relevant but noisier; needs high-precision filtering (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Expertise estimation from Slack](sources/arxiv-watanabe-expertise-estimation-slack.md): 'who knows what' inferred from 27k Slack messages had a best error of 21 points out of 100 (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Encoding Your Domain Expert (Spotify Vedder)](sources/spotify-engineering-vedder-context-layer.md): experts own clusters of datasets, vetted question-SQL pairs and docs; curators rejected 87.5% of examples auto-generated from query history as noise; clusters carry a health score (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Intercom Fin NPI](sources/intercom-fin-npi-agent-readiness.md): a feature counts as shipped only when the support agent can answer about it; a 'what we built' doc plus meeting notes go to an agent that drafts and tests content (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Uber Agentic Pods (CTO post)](sources/x-praveen-uber-agentic-pods.md): engineers shadow domain experts for two days before building, because workflows can't be automated 'by looking at process diagrams or documentation' (first-party) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Internal AI tools for non-engineers (DoP PDF)](sources/departmentofproduct-internal-ai-tools-for-non-engineers.md): a 15-company table; three rows (Spotify, Intercom, Uber) are capture mechanisms (independent summary) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Why Semantic Data Layers matter](sources/departmentofproduct-semantic-data-layers.md): LLM-written metric definitions failed at Anthropic; the rule became "AI drafts, a named human owns the definition". (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

## task-context-isolation: Isolation by task context, not only by user permission
Limiting what a session may combine based on the task (e.g. never two customers' data in one analysis), even when the user could access each separately. Matters for trust/privacy defaults of shared or discoverable sessions.
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): "you shouldn't combine data from two unrelated customer contexts in a single analysis"; the boundary is "what should this task be allowed to view given this context?" (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): tool policies stop sensitive HR data being written to a Stripe-wide doc without banning tools (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How Stripe Built a new Internal AI Knowledge Platform (Department of Product)](sources/departmentofproduct-stripe-kai.md): analogous combination guardrails (two candidates, two patients, performance plus pay) that must be enforced at infrastructure or session level, not by skill owners (independent) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)

## vendor-claims-vs-independent-evidence: Vendor claims dominate; independent evidence is rare
Most evidence on PM agents is vendor marketing or self-reported; controlled or independent evaluations are almost absent. Weigh sources accordingly.
- [River threads jump to 121,804 (Dealroom)](sources/dealroom-river-threads-121804.md): thread volume alone does not prove productivity or quality; no independent impact measure (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify: Building River (ZenML)](sources/zenml-llmops-shopify-river-durable-infrastructure.md): no models, cost, error rates or baselines disclosed (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Building a Public AI Agent Workspace (ZenML)](sources/zenml-llmops-shopify-river-public-workspace.md): security and permission model "aren't described"; the 23% unmerged are not discussed (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Inside Shopify's software factory (Port)](sources/port-software-factories-shopify.md): "1 in 8" has no definition of "coauthored"; best detail comes from press and VC interviews, not the blog (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify's River shows why agent context costs more (Magica)](sources/magica-shopify-river-agent-context-cost.md): no like-for-like comparison against private agents; migration and Aquifer cost undisclosed (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [AI SLOPCAST #9](sources/oleg-guru-ai-slopcast-shopify-river-lehrwerkstatt.md): only positive metrics; review load on seniors unreported (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tobi Lutke: River Now Writes Half (Podcast Alpha)](sources/podcastalpha-tobi-lutke-river-half-of-prs.md): "founder-stated, not audited"; headline overstates Tobi's "up to about 50%... created out of conversations" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How to Make AI Work Visible (MindStudio)](sources/mindstudio-make-ai-work-visible-shopify-river.md): loose restatement used as a product pitch (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Stripe Got 83% of Staff Using One AI Agent. Don't Copy Its Sales Numbers.](sources/aifounders-stripe-kai-dont-copy-sales-numbers.md): independent critique: Kai's +39% deals compares the same sellers' Kai and non-Kai weeks; early adopters are the best sellers; cause open (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Sharadh Krishnamurthy LinkedIn Kai launch post](sources/linkedin-sharadhk-kai-launch-post.md): Kai usage stated as 80% weekly / 20,000+ sessions a day (LinkedIn), 83% (blog), 86%+ (podcast), '>60k sessions' (LangChain): inconsistent bases (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Decision Models Explained - The New AI Building Block for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-decision-models.md): every figure comes from a vendor or CEO, and the leaderboards are only at versions 0.2.1 and 0.3 (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to Build Powerful Internal AI Productivity Tools](sources/departmentofproduct-internal-ai-tools-ramp-glass.md): restates Glass's 350+ skills and its moat claim without data (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Self-improving Product](sources/departmentofproduct-self-improving-product.md): Amplitude Wave reports only ~11% of suggested fixes shipped end to end vs ~50% "would do": an unusually candid vendor number (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to become "AI fluent"](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-fluency.md): relays Fin 86%, Amazon 90% and Stripe 64% figures without question (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to speed up engineering velocity with AI: a non-engineer's guide](sources/departmentofproduct-engineering-velocity-non-engineers.md): Jellyfish, Graphite-at-Shopify (+33% PRs), Glean (-30% turnover) and Morgan Stanley figures repeated unchecked (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Multi Agent Architecture explained](sources/departmentofproduct-multi-agent-architecture.md): Accenture says 10-15% of its clients use multi-agent systems, rising past 30% (WSJ, unchecked) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical Agent Skills for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-practical-agent-skills.md): repeats "Anthropic reporting accuracy went from 21% to 95% with skills" with no source (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to do AI-powered product discovery sprints](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-discovery-sprints.md): repeats Strella's claims (8 weeks down to days; people are more honest with an AI moderator) without checking them (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to test a new AI Model](sources/departmentofproduct-model-sense-testing.md): benchmarks "are often presented in a way that flatters the model" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [ChatPRD guide (Aakash Gupta, with ChatPRD founders)](sources/aakashg-chatprd-guide.md): Not sponsored (stated), but made in collaboration with ChatPRD's Claire Vo and Alisa Haman [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Amplitude AI agents launch](sources/amplitude-ai-agents-launch.md): Launch material; customer counts differ by date (4,500 in Feb 2026 coverage, 4,900 in current boilerplate), both vendor-sourced (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AskNicely cuts analysis time by 75% with Amplitude AI](sources/amplitude-asknicely-story.md): Headline "cuts analysis time by 75%" generalises one self-reported example (dashboard built in under an hour vs about half a day); credited to Amplitude AI Agents, predating the Global Agent launch (case 3) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Intercom customer story (Anthropic)](sources/anthropic-customers-intercom.md): Vendor/partner-sourced resolution rates and customer counts that differ across pages (51%/up to 86% and 25,000+; 76% and 12,000+; 56% and 4,000+) (case 14) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [LLM vs human extraction error rates (arXiv 2508.09458)](sources/arxiv-llm-qualitative-extraction-error-rates.md): Academic preprint (not peer reviewed) rather than vendor claim; not product-specific (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Tempo customer story (Atlassian)](sources/atlassian-tempo-customer-page.md): Banner "30% faster task completion and 3x time savings"; Tempo's own page scopes the 3x to one agent (Structure View Builder) and gives no baseline, sample or period (case 1) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Dovetail case study (AWS)](sources/aws-dovetail-case-study.md): Partner case study, self-reported (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Linear AI agents 2026 guide: 5 alternatives (BuildBetter)](sources/buildbetter-linear-ai-agents-guide.md): Author is a competitor (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Sprig case studies (casestudies.com aggregator)](sources/casestudies-sprig.md): Named results via aggregator; survey-product outcomes, not AI; Nova Credit confirmed on sprig.com (no AI), Chipper Cash/Shift not found on sprig.com (case 12) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Pendo customer story (Claude)](sources/claude-customers-pendo-qa.md): Anthropic customer page; build-stack claim plus a self-reported 90% success on PM-reviewed evals (case 4) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [38 Atlassian AI statistics for 2026](sources/deviniti-atlassian-ai-statistics-2026.md): Every statistic is an Atlassian figure relayed by a services partner, no method; the Procore quote and beta aggregate are NOT in this article (they come from Atlassian's own blog) (case 1) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Dovetail announces world-first AI customer insights hub](sources/dovetail-ai-customer-insights-hub.md): No independent accuracy audit of Dovetail found (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Dovetail Enterprise page](sources/dovetail-enterprise-page.md): Forrester TEI exists but was commissioned by Dovetail (Apr 2025; 236% ROI, composite of 4 interviewees); "30 hrs/user/week" tile not in the TEI summary (unverified) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Notion unveils Custom Agents (ecommercenews.co.nz)](sources/ecommercenews-notion-custom-agents.md): Pigment "70% of employees now using them" (ecommercenews) and Braintrust "20+ minutes saved per Slack update" (Notion customer story) are vendor claims, no method [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Enterpret launches the first agentic customer feedback platform (Business Wire)](sources/enterpret-agentic-feedback-platform-launch.md): Press release (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

- [Notion customer story (Enterpret)](sources/enterpret-notion-customer-story.md): Undefined "360%" headline metric; body gives monthly report 2 weeks to 3 days; cross-attributed quote not found (unverified) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

- [G2 comparison: Productboard vs Zeda.io vs Aha!](sources/g2-productboard-zeda-aha-compare.md): User-review data is the only third-party signal for Aha! AI, and it is thin (search summaries; G2 not fetchable) (case 6) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Sprig reviews (G2)](sources/g2-sprig-reviews.md): Review snippets via search only (G2 blocked fetch, unverified): pricing confusion, oversold no-code event setup, two data-inaccuracy tags (case 12) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Gong product-insight use](sources/gong-product-insights.md): Recipes only; no PM-specific metrics (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Claude Cowork (InfoQ)](sources/infoq-claude-cowork-plugins.md): Vendor docs only (plugin repo README); no outcome data; InfoQ itself does not mention plugins [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Linear Product Intelligence (docs)](sources/linear-product-intelligence-docs.md): Docs/changelog only (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Maze AI moderator](sources/maze-ai-moderator.md): Unattributed "200 interviews in 10 days" (Apr 2026 "AI moderator, expanded" post); named customer LCS gives no quantified after-figure [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

(user-story-mapping)

## work-structure-spectrum: Work structure spectrum (unstructured exploration to task-specific workflow)
Whether a piece of work wants a flexible general harness or a constrained task-specific agent or workflow depends on a handful of properties (step predictability, verifiability, repeatability, error cost, audit need, tacit context), and most real systems are hybrids. Tests Geoff's hypothesis; see tasks/research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy/track-6-work-structure-fit.md.
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): coding work is uniform enough for one agent architecture; knowledge work needs different tools, data, outputs and definitions of done per task (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Production-grade AI agents for financial compliance: Lessons from Stripe](sources/aws-stripe-compliance-agents.md): compliance review decomposed into a DAG of bite-sized, quality-tested sub-questions; the review tool, not an LLM, orchestrates (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe's payment method factory](sources/stripe-payment-method-factory.md): 'although an LLM can orchestrate a workflow, predictable coordination is better implemented in code' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Building effective agents](sources/anthropic-building-effective-agents.md): first-party: workflows (predefined paths) for well-defined tasks, agents for open-ended ones; start simple (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How to think about agent frameworks](sources/langchain-how-to-think-about-agent-frameworks.md): vendor: a spectrum of "how agentic", production systems mix both (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Choose a design pattern for your agentic AI system](sources/google-cloud-choose-design-pattern-agentic-ai.md): vendor: decision table from task traits to pattern; structured single-call work needs no agent (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Best practices for Claude Code](sources/anthropic-claude-code-best-practices.md): first-party: structure is added on demand inside one harness; exploratory tasks may skip planning (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot coding agents](sources/stripe-minions-one-shot-coding-agents.md): first-party: deterministic nodes wrapped around an agentic core for repeatable engineering work (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Orchestrating AI Code Review at scale](sources/cloudflare-ai-code-review-opencode.md): first-party: standardised review as coordinator plus narrow specialists, risk-tiered (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Measuring Agents in Production](sources/arxiv-measuring-agents-in-production.md): independent: deployed agents are short-horizon and human-checked (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Future of Work with AI Agents](sources/arxiv-future-of-work-with-ai-agents.md): independent: Human Agency Scale H1-H5 as a worker-desire axis (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [METR early-2025 developer RCT](sources/metr-early-2025-experienced-developer-rct.md): independent: tacit-context, high-standard work saw slowdown with a general assistant (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Anthropic Economic Index, January 2026](sources/anthropic-economic-index-2026-01.md): first-party: Claude.ai 52% augmentation; API about 75% automation (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Ask HN: non-coding workflows](sources/hn-ask-claude-code-non-coding-workflows.md): anecdote: unstructured personal knowledge work runs in a general coding harness with folder structure (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Boris Cherny summary (Traces)](sources/traces-boris-cherny-light-cone-summary.md): second-hand counter-evidence: model-compensating structure is temporary (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Are Agent Harnesses the new "secret sauce" for Product Teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-harnesses-secret-sauce.md): Stripe Minions blueprints and GitHub Copilot's mandatory CodeQL and secret scanning as "mix AI steps with fixed rules" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Perplexity's new Computer...](sources/departmentofproduct-perplexity-computer.md): outcome-first planning with sub-agents, plus persistent background workers on triggers that run "indefinitely" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to Identify Opportunities for AI Automation](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-automation-opportunities.md): scores each task 1-3 on safety, volume and verifiability, giving three outcomes: automate now, AI assistant, or not ready. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Agentic Workflows Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-agentic-workflows-explained.md): deterministic automation vs non-deterministic agentic workflow as the first mental model, with a seven-part anatomy. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use /loops, /goals and other Powerful Slash Commands as a Non-Engineer](sources/departmentofproduct-loops-goals-slash-commands.md): steps of structure inside one harness: a prompt, then a goal (a stated "done" condition), then a loop that calls a reusable command file (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Claude Cowork as a Competitive Intelligence System](sources/departmentofproduct-cowork-competitive-intelligence.md): a user-defined phrase ("Run the intel workflow") reruns the whole chain, adding structure on demand inside a general agent (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Strategy Thought Partner](sources/departmentofproduct-strategy-thought-partner.md): product frameworks supply the structure. A recommender picks 3, then the chosen framework scripts a step-by-step sparring conversation (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What is a Jira space (formerly project)](sources/atlassian-jira-space-definition.md): team-managed (each team controls its own config) vs company-managed (admin-standardised) is a built-in structured-vs-flexible dial. (user-story-mapping)
- [What is a Confluence space](sources/atlassian-confluence-space-definition.md): a space is a loose knowledge container (knowledge base, launch or campaign space) with no enforced artifact types. (user-story-mapping)
- [What is an idea (Jira Product Discovery docs)](sources/atlassian-jira-product-discovery-ideas.md): connection fields (Premium) link ideas without imposing a fixed hierarchy. (user-story-mapping)
- [Working with databases (Notion API docs)](sources/notion-api-databases-data-sources.md): databases give typed structure, pages give free-form body, in the same object. (user-story-mapping)
- [Projects (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-projects.md): strong opinionated structure (one issue in one project; lead team sets statuses). (user-story-mapping)
- [Initiatives (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-initiatives.md): initiative > project > issue, with team-led sub-initiatives rolling up to company goals. (user-story-mapping)
- [Add features to your hierarchy (Productboard support)](sources/productboard-product-hierarchy.md): Hierarchy: Product > Component > Feature > Subfeature. Features can be imported from spreadsheet, Jira or Zapier. (user-story-mapping)
- [About Projects (GitHub Docs)](sources/github-docs-about-projects.md): items are issues, PRs or draft issues with up to 50 custom fields; table, board and roadmap views. (user-story-mapping)
